prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1358; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured. Insured states a vehicle crossed into their lane on a two-lane road at approximately 10 mph. Both vehicles were driven away from the scene under their own power. Claimant reports headache and dizziness and was transported to urgent care by family. Claimant is not represented by counsel. Photos requested from both parties; police report number pending.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant confirms a concussion diagnosis from the treating clinic and reports ongoing headaches, light sensitivity, and difficulty concentrating at work. Claimant asked what the claims process involves and was advised that medical records and bills are needed to evaluate the bodily injury portion. Provided a list of required documents and explained that claimant may seek independent advice at any time.

Entry 3: Received the police report from the responding agency. Report notes minor front bumper damage to both vehicles and no citations issued. Other driver's statement says the claimant's vehicle drifted into the oncoming lane. Statements conflict on lane position; noted for liability review. Vehicle inspection scheduled with the appraiser to confirm damage consistent with a low-speed impact.

Entry 4: Medical records received from the claimant's neurologist. Records document a concussion with post-concussive symptoms and a referral to vision therapy. Claimant's treating physician estimates recovery over several weeks to months. Reviewed records with the medical reviewer, who confirmed the diagnosis is consistent with the reported mechanism of injury. Claimant has not yet returned to full work duties.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant to check on symptom progress and confirm receipt of the document checklist. Claimant reports symptoms are slowly improving but still present. Reminded claimant of the option to consult an attorney or a public adjuster, and that the claim file will remain open pending final medical update. Next review scheduled for the end of the treatment period.
